items.title: Peter Bocage Interview, 1959-01-29
items.q: I played with him a lot too.

ctx.x: Well, I don't know. It's practically, you take certain types now. You take Bolden and, say, Freddie Keppert, now he died in Chicago. They were mostly on the same style. They were powerful trumpet players and they mostly, well, the improvisation is always going to be a little different, you know, and they're no two men alike, you understand? But it's the similarity there, you understand what I mean, between them and the style was just a forceful trumpet player, you understand? Just strong and came out.

Well, Joe was good too. Joe was very good. I played with him a lot too. Well, Joe was powerful. He didn't have too much of a tone, but he was good for jazz because he could make all that, he could make it go like a dog and all that, you understand? You know, that wah-wah stuff and he'd make all that on the horn, you know? And he was strong, you know, he's a big fella, as big as you, you know? You saw him, huh? No. You ever seen? Same picture, he's a terrible picture. Yeah, he was a very big fella. I got a picture…
